findings.what: answerOf hard-codes 'The API answered 201' instead of the status received; the receipts also fall back to literal 200 (line 161) and 201 (line 190)
findings.why: HONEST-1: no number the data doesn't hold. react-web: every value comes from the API's answer. The status is in cancelling.status, but the header writes its own. The fallbacks can't be reached, but they are invented values.

findings.what: Header 'Policy status' comes from one GET on mount, so after a 201 cancel on the same screen it still shows the pre-cancel status (e.g. Active)
findings.why: WB-4 shows a successful cancel; HONEST-1: a status shown must be the one the API holds now. A re-read after the 201, or labelling the status as of load, would keep it honest.

findings.what: Local ruleHref = '#/rules/' + ruleId, unencoded, a new copy beside src/web/app/shell/ruleLinks.ts
findings.why: Same issue as U7's 'one shared helper builds every workbench rule link' (W1 review A3 R3). This adds another instance for that line to cover, rather than a new blocker. Rule of three: this is a third or later copy.

findings.what: The 'quote and cancellation agree (068)' unit test feeds two recorded answers through a pass-through client and compares them: it proves the fixture, not the code
findings.why: Anti-oracle: the client doesn't decide agreement, so this test can't fail for a code fault. The live e2e comparison tests do prove WB-4's 'agree', so coverage isn't lost.
